steps.name: DESeq2 differential expression: treated vs control
caveats: At 3 replicates per group the test has low power; most true effects found will have large fold changes and many true positives will be missed
steps.context: 12000 x 6 raw Salmon gene-level counts, Ensembl Danio rerio annotation. 3 treated vs 3 control, unpaired, single batch, no covariates.
steps.question: Which of the 12,000 zebrafish genes are significantly differentially expressed between drug-treated and control larvae pools (treated vs control, control as reference level)?

grounding.reason: DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm shrinkage, explicit reference level, BH/independent filtering at alpha 0.05, per the grounded two-group DESeq2 procedure.

constraints: Do not scale/normalize counts prior to DESeq2 — normalization is internal via size factors
Set reference level explicitly (control) rather than relying on alphabetical default
Keep alpha at 0.05 default; do not tighten/loosen the threshold to compensate for small n
Do not filter results by unadjusted p-value or by fold change alone
acceptance_criteria: Genes pre-filtered to >=10 counts in >=3 samples (the smallest group size)
DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors used for normalization internally (no pre-normalization of counts)
Design ~condition with condition releveled so 'control' is the explicit reference; contrast reported as condition treated vs control
Wald test run; apeglm shrinkage applied to log2FoldChange for the treated-vs-control coefficient
Results table reports both unshrunken and shrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE, raw p-value, and BH-adjusted p-value (padj) per gene
Genes selected as DE at padj < 0.05 (independent filtering on, alpha=0.05 passed to results())
p-value histogram inspected and reported before trusting BH adjustment
MA plot and dispersion plot produced as fit diagnostics
Count-outlier-flagged genes (Cook's distance NA p-values) reported separately from independent-filtering NAs

Report explicitly states the low-power caveat of n=3 per group: only a minority of true DE genes are expected to be detected, biased toward large fold changes; absence from the list is not evidence of no effect

steps.name: Map zebrafish genes to human orthologs
caveats: An ortholog map drops every zebrafish gene without a clean one-to-one human ortholog; this share should be reported as a real analysis limitation, not glossed over
steps.context: The environment holds no zebrafish-specific curated pathway gene set collection (WikiPathways and MSigDB collections staged here are human, mouse, or rat only). org.Dr.eg.db (Bioconductor, zebrafish annotation) is available for ID mapping to human orthologs; NCBI gene identifier files for human and zebrafish gene2ensembl cross-references are also staged as a fallback/cross-check.
steps.question: What is the best available human ortholog for each of the tested zebrafish genes, so that human curated pathway collections can be used for enrichment?

grounding.reason: R-0050/R-0081: for an organism other than human/mouse with no curated gene set collection, map genes to human orthologs (or use GO) and state the path and its coverage limit.

constraints: State the ortholog mapping source and version in the report
Do not silently drop the mapping-loss count — report it beside the enrichment results
Resolve many-to-many mappings by an explicit, stated rule rather than arbitrarily
acceptance_criteria: Zebrafish gene symbols/IDs from the DESeq2 results table mapped to human Entrez/HGNC symbols using org.Dr.eg.db and/or the NCBI gene identifier cross-reference tables for zebrafish/human
Mapping report states: number of tested zebrafish genes, number successfully mapped to a one-to-one human ortholog, number dropped (no ortholog or ambiguous many-to-many), and the mapped share

Output is a ranked list keyed by human gene symbol with the DESeq2 Wald statistic carried over, one row per successfully mapped ortholog (ties/duplicates resolved by keeping the most significant zebrafish gene per human symbol, stated explicitly)

constraints: Rank by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (stat column), not by unshrunken log2FC alone and not by a signed p-value with ties

acceptance_criteria: Full ranked list of ortholog-mapped genes (all tested genes, no significance pre-filter) ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic used as fgsea input

fgsea run against MSigDB Hallmark human gene sets and WikiPathways human gene sets (both staged in the reference store), gene set size window 15-500 members after intersecting with the tested/mapped gene universe
BH-adjusted p-values (padj) reported per gene set; redundant/highly overlapping significant sets collapsed to one representative per group, full table kept as supplement
Leading-edge genes reported for each significant gene set, with overlap between leading edges of different significant sets noted

If fewer than ~50 zebrafish genes are DE at padj<0.05, no over-representation analysis is run on that short list — GSEA on the full ranked list is the sole enrichment method, and the DE-list size is stated

plan.title: Zebrafish larvae drug exposure DE + pathway analysis
plan.analytical_narrative: 12,000-gene Salmon-quantified count matrix from 3 drug-treated vs 3 control zebrafish larvae pools (whole larvae, single batch, unpaired). The plan follows the grounded DESeq2 procedure: sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA, sample distance heatmap) to check the 3-vs-3 design clusters as expected and to flag any outlier pool before testing; a minimal low-count pre-filter; DESeq2 median-of-ratios normalization built into the model; a Wald test on an explicit condition factor (control as reference) with apeglm-shrunken log2 fold changes and BH-adjusted p-values (alpha 0.05, independent filtering on); and a preranked fgsea pathway analysis on the Wald statistic. Because zebrafish is not a species this environment holds a curated MSigDB collection for, gene symbols are mapped to human orthologs (via org.Dr.eg.db / NCBI gene identifier cross-references) before running enrichment against the MSigDB Hallmark human and WikiPathways human gene sets staged in the reference store; the ortholog mapping's coverage loss and the standing low-power caveat of an n=3 design are both carried into the final report rather than dropped silently.
